prompt: Should we use event sourcing or CRUD for our order management system? We expect ~1000 orders/day, need audit trails, and may add a recommendation engine later.

approaches.name: CRUD with audit log
pros: Familiar to the team — Django ORM is purpose-built for CRUD
PostgreSQL triggers or Django signals can capture changes for audit
Low learning curve, fast time to market
cons: Audit log is a bolt-on, not native to the data model
Harder to replay history or reconstruct past states
May need refactoring if event-driven features grow significantly

approaches.name: Event sourcing
pros: Complete audit trail is inherent — every state change is an event
Natural fit for the future recommendation engine (event stream as input)
Enables temporal queries and state reconstruction
Audit trail and event stream are first-class citizens
Natural fit for temporal queries and state reconstruction
Recommendation engine gets a native event stream
cons: Steep learning curve for a team with no ES experience
Requires new infrastructure (event store, projections, possibly CQRS)
Django ORM is not designed for event sourcing — fighting the framework
Significantly more complex for 1000 orders/day which doesn't demand it
Team has no ES experience — high ramp-up cost
Django and PostgreSQL are not natural ES tools
CQRS adds operational complexity (projections, eventual consistency)

approaches.name: CRUD with domain events
pros: Keeps the familiar Django CRUD model the team knows
Domain events (published via Celery) provide an event stream for the recommendation engine
Audit trail via a changes table with before/after snapshots
Incremental path — can evolve toward event sourcing later if needed
cons: Dual-write concern: must ensure both the CRUD update and event publish succeed
Audit trail is still a secondary concern, not the primary data model
Domain events need schema versioning as the system evolves

approaches.name: Plain CRUD
cons: No audit trail without additional work
No event stream for future recommendation engine

summary.synthesis: For a team of 3 with Django expertise and no event sourcing experience, CRUD with a dedicated audit log table is the pragmatic choice. The order volume (1000/day) doesn't justify the complexity of event sourcing. If the recommendation engine later needs an event stream, you can publish domain events from the CRUD layer without fully adopting event sourcing. CRUD with domain events strikes the best balance: it leverages the team's Django expertise, provides an audit trail, and creates the event stream the recommendation engine will need — all without the complexity of full event sourcing. Use Django signals to publish order events to a Celery queue, and store audit snapshots in a dedicated table. This positions you to evolve toward event sourcing incrementally if scale demands it.
